subject: Eval runbook + variant scorecard / close timeline (MAP)
messages:
From: hannah schmitt <hannah.s@redwood.ai>
To: Sally Brown <sally.brown@acmehealth.com>
Cc: karthik iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, jonas weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Eval runbook proposal and benchmark scope

Hi Sally,

Thanks again for the sync this morning. As discussed, I've attached a short runbook that lays out the MAP milestones and the performance benchmarking plan we propose to validate Redwood for your document ingestion pipeline use case.

High-level plan (week-by-week):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize MAP + data profiles, decide model variants to test
- Week 1: lab-scale runs (1–8 concurrent clients) — latency, TTFT, per-token cost
- Week 2: scale runs (16–128 concurrency across 4 regions) — throughput and KV cache behavior
- Week 3: regressions and quality checks (NLP evals on your prompt set), produce final scorecard

Benchmark axes we'll measure:
- P50/P90/P95 token latency (generation start) and TTFT (time-to-first-token)
- Throughput (tokens/sec) at target concurrency
- Memory/KV-hit rates and effective batching efficiency
- Quality metrics: exact-match / ROUGE-like aggregate on your eval set

Model variants (candidate list):
- gpt-open-13b-16k (FP16) — baseline quality
- gpt-open-6b-q4_0 — quantized, lower cost
- redwood-v1.1-13b — our Redwood-special tuned variant

Deliverables: MAP, runbook, raw CSV results, variant scorecard PDF, SLA draft for procurement.

Can you confirm the availability of a representative prompt set and a small sample of production traffic (anonymized) by Wednesday? We'll then pencil in the lab runs for next week.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: map-runbook-v1.pdf (proposal), sample-config.yaml (stub)

From: Sally Brown <sally.brown@acmehealth.com>
To: hannah schmitt <hannah.s@redwood.ai>
Cc: jonas weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, karthik iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 08:23:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MAP: Eval runbook proposal and benchmark scope

Appreciate the thorough plan, Hannah — this looks like what we need.

A couple quick asks from our side before you run:
1) For TTFT, can you measure cold-start vs warm (i.e., after KV cache priming)? Our latency SLO is p95 < 400ms for first token on standard requests, and we'd like to see warm/cold split.
2) On concurrency, our production PVC scales up to ~64 concurrent active sessions during peak — can you include a 64-concurrency bucket in the scale runs?

I'll get you an anonymized prompt set and a 24-hour traffic dump by end of day Wednesday. Procurement (procurement@acmehealth.com) will review any SLA language; copying Michael from procurement who will own the PO.

Sally Brown
Head of AI Product
Acme Health

From: karthik iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: hannah schmitt <hannah.s@redwood.ai>, jonas weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Eval runbook proposal and benchmark scope

Notes for the runbook execution — pushing a quick test matrix so we can automate the runs:

Test matrix (per model variant):
- Concurrency buckets: 1, 4, 16, 64, 128
- Prompt length buckets (tokens): 32, 128, 512
- Sequence length assumed: up to 4k
- Metrics captured: TTFT (cold/warm), p50/p90/p95 latency, tokens/sec, CPU/GPU utilization, KV hit rate

Automation plan:
- Use the Redwood perf harness with realistic jitter and prefix caching enabled
- Warm runs: pre-prime KV cache with 100 representative sessions
- Cold runs: spin fresh workers, measure TTFT first token

Estimate: full sweep across 3 variants and matrix above ~ 18 hours on a 4-GPU cluster (we'll reserve Dedicated capacity for the run).

I'll template the CSV header and post the results into the shared Drive link once done.

-k
Karthik Iyer
Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: perf-matrix-template.csv (stub)

From: hannah schmitt <hannah.s@redwood.ai>
To: Sally Brown <sally.brown@acmehealth.com>
Cc: karthik iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, jonas weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Eval runbook proposal and benchmark scope

Sally —

We completed the lab sweep this morning and attached the run results and a short scorecard comparing model variants.

Executive summary (high level):
- Redwood-v1.1-13b (FP16) — best quality / balanced latency: p95 TTFT warm=320ms, p95 end-to-end=610ms at 64 concurrency; cost ~1.0x baseline.
- gpt-open-13b-16k (FP16) — similar quality, slightly higher variance under sustained load: p95 TTFT warm=360ms; better throughput at 128 conc but higher p95 under cold starts.
- gpt-open-6b-q4_0 — cost-efficient: p95 TTFT warm=480ms, end-to-end p95=920ms at 64 conc; quality delta on your eval prompts ~6% lower on intent-match.

Notes:
- Cold-start TTFTs are ~1.7x warm for all variants; priming your hot set reduces p95 substantially.
- Batching efficiency improved with prefix caching; effective tokens/sec increased ~25% when cache hit rate >70%.

Attached:
- map-performance-results.csv (raw runs)
- variant-diffs.pdf (scorecard with tradeoff plots)
- redwood-sla-draft.docx (SLA + pricing for Dedicated capacity)

Next steps we'd like:
1) Internal sign-off from your product and procurement on the MAP and SLA draft
2) PO / DocuSign for Dedicated reservation so we can schedule a canary roll the week after approval
3) Quick 30-min review call to walk through the PDF scorecard — propose Thu 10/22 9:00am PT

Thanks again — happy to adjust the runs if you want an expanded variant sweep.

Best,
Hannah

Attachments: map-performance-results.csv, variant-diffs.pdf, redwood-sla-draft.docx
